delete.description: [Feature-gated: enable_simulation_delete] Permanently deletes a simulation and all associated data including results, logs, and checkpoints. This action cannot be undone. Running simulations must be terminated before deletion. This endpoint is only available on deployments where the enable_simulation_delete feature flag is enabled; callers may receive 404 on deployments where the flag is off.

parameters.name: sim_id
parameters.description: Simulation ID in `sim_xxx` format

400.description: Invalid simulation ID format

post.description: Initiates graceful termination of a running simulation. The simulation will transition to `terminated` status. Results generated up to the termination point will be available.

parameters.name: sim_id
parameters.description: Simulation ID in `sim_xxx` format

202.description: Termination dispatched for a simulation whose workspace has been deleted. Returned without a body: workspace deletion revokes the simulation's details, so the acknowledgement carries no SimulationDetails payload. Also returned when the backend refuses the request with a 4xx, whose message would describe the revoked simulation; a backend 5xx is reported as itself.

400.description: Bad Request - Invalid simulation ID format, or the simulation has no platform link and cannot be terminated

409.description: Conflict - Simulation is not in a running state

501.description: Not Implemented - Termination is not yet supported for this simulation's backend

503.description: Service Unavailable - The termination transport is unavailable

post.summary: Submit a collective-operation workload for simple network simulation
post.description: Validates the workload against operation/algorithm compatibility rules, resolves or synthesizes a topology and traceset, creates a configuration, and launches a simulation. Returns immediately with status `accepted`; poll `GET /api/v1/simulations/{simulationId}` to track progress. Note: the poll response uses a different schema (`SimulationDetails`) — the simulation ID is returned as `id` (not `simulationId`), the workload is not echoed back, and the status transitions from `accepted` to `provisioning` on the next poll. Identical workloads are deduplicated via content-addressed tracesets.

mixed_parallel_groups.summary: Multiple group specs with different operations

400.description: Validation error — invalid rank count, unsupported operation/algorithm combination, both topology and topologyConstraints set, or constraint solver cannot satisfy the request

invalid_ranks.summary: Rank count not in reference set (no constraints)

error.message: algorithm 'ring' is not compatible with operation 'allToAll'; allowed algorithms: sequential, interleaved
topologyConstraints and topology are mutually exclusive

post.summary: Preview the derived topology for a simple simulation request
post.description: Runs the full validation and topology derivation pipeline against the provided workload or groups, then returns the physical network topology that would be produced — without creating a simulation, traceset, or configuration. The request body is identical to POST /api/v1/simple/simulations. The workload/groups payload is required because the total rank count drives topology derivation (rack count, tier selection, switch allocation), but no workload details are echoed in the response. The response describes only the physical network: tier structure, switch counts, link counts, data rates, and resolved constraint values.

400.description: Validation error — identical to POST /api/v1/simple/simulations

invalid_ranks.summary: Rank count not in reference set (no constraints)

get.description: Returns the full compatibility matrix mapping each collective operation type to its allowed algorithms, platform default, and power-of-two constraints. This is a static reference endpoint — the matrix does not change between requests.

TracesetItem.description: Traceset item in configuration tracesets list response

hash.description: Content hash (crc64nvme format). Null or omitted while ingest is in progress and the library row has not yet been written; clients must treat absence and explicit null as equivalent.

hashShort.description: Short hash for display (12 Unicode scalar values from the start of `hash`). Null or omitted when `hash` is not yet available; clients must treat absence and explicit null as equivalent.

totalSize.description: Total size in bytes. Null or omitted when the library row has not yet been written; clients must treat absence and explicit null as equivalent. Tracesets routinely exceed 2 GB, so this must be int64 (the generator only honors format:int64 with single-type integer + nullable:true, not the type-array form).

format.description: Trace format. Null or omitted when the library row has not yet been written; clients must treat absence and explicit null as equivalent. Encoded as `oneOf` with explicit `type:'null'` because `nullable:true` on an enum is silently dropped by the openapi-python-client generator (it emits `Enum(value)` direct construction and crashes on JSON null). The `oneOf` form forces the codegen to emit a None-guarded `_parse_format` helper.

metadataStatus.description: Metadata extraction status. Null or omitted when the library row has not yet been written; clients must treat absence and explicit null as equivalent. Encoded as `oneOf` with explicit `type:'null'` for the same reason as `format` — to force null-safe Python codegen on a nullable enum.

ActiveTraceset.description: Active traceset reference for chakra-based simulations. Contains both the name (for human readability and V1 WorkloadName) and ID (for unambiguous identification).

name.description: Human-readable traceset name, used for V1 WorkloadName

simulatedTime.description: Maximum simulated network time reached. Format: '{value} {unit}' where unit is 'us', 'ms', or 's' (e.g., '1.50 ms', '0.42 us', '3.20 s').

eventsProcessed.description: Total packets (tx + rx) across all network interfaces at the final simulated timestamp.

throughput.description: Average transmit throughput across all interfaces and timesteps. Format: '{value} Gbps' (e.g., '0.14 Gbps').

name.description: File path relative to the simulation's results prefix. Nested files include their subdirectory (e.g. "subdir/file.csv"); top-level files are just the file name. SECURITY: this value can contain '/' and is NOT a safe basename — consumers that write results to the filesystem MUST NOT path-join it onto a destination directory without re-validating (reject '.'/'..' segments, absolute paths). Sanitize to a basename or apply an equivalent relative-path check before any filesystem operation.

failureReason.description: Reason the simulation failed. Only present when status is 'failed'.

metrics.description: Simulation metrics computed from nd-stats output. Only present for terminal simulations that produced simulation results. Null means either the simulation did not produce results (e.g., failed before running) or results are still being exported. Check the simulation status and startedAt field to distinguish.

name.description: Simulation name. SECURITY: this value is interpolated into command strings and Slurm entrypoints executed on cluster nodes, so it is restricted to letters, digits, '-' and '_' (1–255 characters), and must start with a letter or digit (no whitespace, other punctuation, or non-ASCII characters, and no leading '-' or '_').

FileDownloadUrlResponse.description: Response containing a presigned download URL for a simulation result file

fileName.description: Path of the result file relative to the simulation's results prefix; nested files include their subdirectory (e.g. "subdir/file.csv"). Echoes the requested fileName. SECURITY: this value can contain '/' and is NOT a safe basename — consumers that write to the filesystem MUST re-validate (reject '.'/'..' segments, absolute paths) or sanitize to a basename before path-joining.

checksum.description: Algorithm-tagged checksum of the file (e.g. `md5:<hex>`, `crc64nvme:<base64url>`). Omitted when no verifiable whole-file checksum is available (multipart uploads without CRC64NVME, SSE-KMS/SSE-C objects). Integrity only — not a cryptographic authenticity mechanism.

downloadUrl.description: Presigned S3 URL for downloading the file

expiresAt.description: Expiration time of the presigned URL (15 minutes from generation)

SummaryResponse.description: Response containing computed summary data for simulation results with a presigned download URL for the zstd-compressed JSON summary

SummaryFileInfo.description: File information with presigned download URL for the summary data

downloadUrl.description: Presigned S3 URL for downloading the summary file

expiresAt.description: Expiration time of the presigned URL

cached.description: Whether this summary was served from cache

computedAt.description: When this summary was computed (omitted if cached)

rowsProcessed.description: Number of CSV rows processed (omitted if cached or zero)

computeTimeMs.description: Time taken to compute in milliseconds (omitted if cached or zero)

TracesetPagination.description: Cursor-based pagination for trace-service list endpoints.

WorkloadMetadata.description: Workload characterization metadata attached to a traceset on promotion. The canonical structure is owned by trace-service (see trace-service/openapi.json#WorkloadMetadata); this central-side schema is intentionally permissive (no `properties`, no `additionalProperties` constraint — accepts any JSON object shape) so customers can read whatever the trace-service emits without spec drift breaking SDK decoding. `additionalProperties: true` is omitted deliberately — the scala-openapi generator rejects that form unless paired with a `$ref` value type.

role.description: Role of the file in the traceset

TracesetResponse.description: Full traceset detail. On public-scope tracesets, the server intentionally omits tenant-identifying fields (workspaceId, promotedBy) per §5.1/§6.4 — clients must treat them as optional and tolerate absence.

workspaceId.description: Owning workspace ID. Omitted on public-scope tracesets per tenant-stripping rules; clients must treat the field as optional and tolerate its absence.

workloadMetadata.description: Workload characterization metadata. Present only after promotion; omitted otherwise. Encoded as `oneOf` with explicit `type:'null'` because `nullable:true` adjacent to `$ref` is ignored by the OpenAPI Python generator (the $ref form short-circuits sibling keywords), causing it to emit `WorkloadMetadata.from_dict(value)` without a None guard and crash on JSON null. The `oneOf` form forces the codegen to emit the null branch.

rankCountDerived.description: Rank count derived from workloadMetadata parallelism config. Omitted when not derivable.

promotedAt.description: Timestamp at which the traceset was last promoted. Omitted for un-promoted tracesets.

promotedBy.description: User who promoted the traceset. Omitted on public-scope tracesets per tenant-stripping rules.

role.description: Role of the file in the traceset

workspaceId.description: Workspace ID. If not provided, uses the universal traceset workspace.

ttlDays.description: Custom TTL in days (1-365). Uses server default if omitted.

role.description: Role of the file in the traceset

SimpleOperationType.description: MPI collective operation type for simple network simulation workloads.

SimpleAlgorithm.description: Collective expansion algorithm. If omitted, the platform default for the selected operation is used. Names follow MPI/NCCL conventions where applicable. Domain synonyms are accepted on input: rabenseifner → recursiveHalvingDoubling, pairwiseExchange → sequential, pipelinedPairwise → interleaved, flat/linear → direct, recursiveHalving → halving.

SimpleWorkloadPhase.description: A single collective operation phase within a workload. Each phase specifies an operation type, optional algorithm override, and data size.

algorithm.description: Algorithm for this phase. If omitted, the platform default for the operation is used.

dataSize.description: Data size in bytes for this phase.

SimpleWorkload.description: Sequential workload specification. All ranks execute the same ordered phases. Mutually exclusive with groups. Not all algorithms are valid for every operation; see GET /api/v1/simple/compatibility for the full operation/algorithm compatibility matrix including defaults and power-of-two constraints.

ranks.description: Number of participating ranks. Without topologyConstraints, must be one of the reference topology sizes: 4, 8, 16, 32, 64, 128, 256, 512, 1024, 2048, 4096. Large sizes (8192, 16384, 32768, 65536) require the enable_large_simple_sim_topologies flag. With topologyConstraints, any positive value satisfying the constraint solver is accepted.

phases.description: Ordered list of collective operation phases (1–16). Operations execute sequentially via ctrlDeps chaining.

SimpleGroupSpec.description: Specification for a group of ranks running the same collective operations concurrently with other groups. Multiple groups with the same spec create independent process groups on disjoint rank ranges.

count.description: Number of identical groups to create.

phases.description: Operations each group executes (sequentially within group, parallel across groups).

SimpleSimulationMode.description: Execution mode of a simple simulation. Sequential: all ranks execute the same phases via a single process group. Parallel: ranks are partitioned into independent groups that execute concurrently.

TopologyConstraints.description: Hardware constraints for topology derivation. The solver derives a valid CLOS topology from the specified switch radix and oversubscription ratio. A 2-tier topology is used when ranks fit within the radix capacity (ports × hosts_per_leaf); otherwise a 3-tier pod-based topology (RSW → FSW → SSW) is derived with all switches fully utilized. When present, rank count is not restricted to the reference values — any count satisfying the constraints is valid.

switchRadix.description: Switch port configuration for TH5-class (51200 Gbps switching capacity). Format: PortsxSpeed (e.g. 128x400G). 64x800G: 64 ports at 800 Gbps. 128x400G: 128 ports at 400 Gbps (default). 256x200G: 256 ports at 200 Gbps.

subscriptionRatio.description: Target oversubscription ratio (downlink BW : uplink BW) applied at every switch tier. 1:1: equal uplink and downlink bandwidth (default). 2:1, 3:1, and 4:1: more downlink capacity, fewer uplinks. The ratio is applied to both rack switches (RSW) and fabric switches (FSW) in 3-tier topologies. Actual ratios may differ slightly from the target due to integer port rounding.

nicNetworkPortSpeed.description: NIC network port speed in Gbps. Determines the data rate of each host-to-switch connection. When omitted, defaults to the switch link speed from switchRadix (e.g. 400 for 128x400G). The effective link speed between a NIC and its rack switch is min(nicNetworkPortSpeed, switchLinkSpeed) — the lower of the two is used for both topology capacity planning and the generated configuration. PCIe generation is auto-selected to match the effective NIC speed. Allowed values: 50, 100, 200, 400, 800 Gbps.

SimpleSimulationRequest.description: Request to create a simple collective-operation simulation. Exactly one of workload or groups must be specified.

name.description: Optional human-readable name for the simulation. Auto-generated when omitted. SECURITY: this value is interpolated into command strings and Slurm entrypoints executed on cluster nodes, so it is restricted to letters, digits, '-' and '_' (1–255 characters), and must start with a letter or digit (no whitespace, other punctuation, or non-ASCII characters, and no leading '-' or '_').

topology.description: Optional topology reference (reserved for K2 orchestration).

topologyConstraints.description: Hardware constraints for topology derivation. Mutually exclusive with topology.

workload.description: Sequential workload: all ranks execute the same phases. Mutually exclusive with groups.

groups.description: Parallel groups: ranks partitioned into independent groups executing concurrently. Mutually exclusive with workload.

SimpleSimulationStatus.description: Status of a simple simulation submission.

simulationId.description: Unique identifier for the submitted simulation.

workload.description: Resolved workload with algorithms filled in. Present when mode is sequential.

groups.description: Resolved groups with algorithms filled in. Present when mode is parallel.

TopologyTier.description: Switch details for a single tier of the CLOS topology. Tiers are ordered bottom-up: RSW (rack), FSW (fabric), SSW (spine).

name.description: Switch role at this tier. RSW = rack switch (leaf), FSW = fabric switch, SSW = spine switch (super-spine).

switchCount.description: Total number of switches at this tier.

downlinksPerSwitch.description: Number of downlink ports per switch. For RSW: host-facing ports. For FSW: RSW-facing ports. For SSW: FSW-facing ports.

uplinksPerSwitch.description: Number of uplink ports per switch. For RSW: FSW-facing ports. For FSW: SSW-facing ports. 0 for the top-of-tree tier.

downlinkDataRateGbps.description: Data rate on each downlink in Gbps. For RSW downlinks, this is min(nicNetworkPortSpeed, switchLinkSpeed) — the effective host-to-switch speed.

uplinkDataRateGbps.description: Data rate on each uplink in Gbps. 0 for the top-of-tree tier (no uplinks).

effectiveSubscriptionRatio.description: Effective oversubscription ratio at this tier in N:1 notation (e.g., '1:1', '2:1', '1.91:1'), computed from actual port counts and data rates: (downlinks × downlinkRate) / (uplinks × uplinkRate). May differ from the target ratio due to integer port rounding. Null for the top-of-tree tier (no uplinks).

switchCapacityUtilization.description: Percentage of the switch's total switching capacity consumed by connected links at this tier. Computed as (downlinks × downlinkRate + uplinks × uplinkRate) / switchingCapacityGbps × 100. For example, a fully packed 128×400G switch (51200 Gbps) shows 100.0. Under-packed switches or non-standard NIC speeds produce lower values.

TopologyLinks.description: Aggregate link counts at each tier boundary of the topology.

hostToRsw.description: Total host-to-RSW links. Equals totalHosts (one NIC per host).

rswToFsw.description: Total RSW-to-FSW links (RSW count times uplinks per RSW). 0 for 1-tier topologies.

fswToSsw.description: Total FSW-to-SSW links (FSW count times uplinks per FSW). 0 for 1-tier and 2-tier topologies.

ResolvedConstraints.description: The constraint values actually used for topology derivation, including defaults applied when the user omitted a field. For reference topologies (no topologyConstraints in request), shows the equivalent 128x400G / 1:1 defaults.

nicNetworkPortSpeed.description: Configured NIC network port speed in Gbps. This is the value the user requested, or the switch link speed if omitted.

effectiveNicSpeed.description: Effective NIC-to-switch link speed in Gbps: min(nicNetworkPortSpeed, switchLinkSpeed). When the NIC speed exceeds the switch port speed, the link operates at the slower switch speed. This is the data rate used for RSW downlinks and topology capacity planning.

switchLinkSpeed.description: Switch link speed in Gbps, derived from switchRadix (e.g., 400 for 128x400G).

switchingCapacityGbps.description: Total switching capacity per switch in Gbps. All current switch models are 51200 Gbps (TH5-class).

TopologyPreview.description: Derived physical network topology details. Describes the CLOS fabric structure that would be produced for a simulation with the given inputs. This is a pure computation result — no simulation or configuration is created.

tierCount.description: Number of switch tiers. 1 = single rack (RSW only), 2 = leaf-spine (RSW + FSW), 3 = pod-based (RSW + FSW + SSW).

totalHosts.description: Total host count in the topology. Equals total ranks for sequential mode or sum of (count * groupSize) for parallel mode.

ranksPerHost.description: Number of ranks mapped to each host. Currently always 1.

ranksPerRack.description: Number of ranks (hosts) per rack. Equals the RSW downlink count — each host connects to its rack switch via one NIC port.

tiers.description: Per-tier switch details, ordered bottom-up (RSW first, then FSW, then SSW). Array length equals tierCount.

links.description: Aggregate link counts at each tier boundary.

resolvedConstraints.description: The constraint values used for derivation, including defaults applied for omitted fields.

pods.description: Number of pods in the topology. Present only for 3-tier topologies (tierCount = 3).

racksPerPod.description: Number of racks per pod. Present only for 3-tier topologies (tierCount = 3).

spinePlanes.description: Number of independent spine planes. The preprocessor divides SSWs across planes and assigns FSWs round-robin. Present only for 3-tier topologies (tierCount = 3).

TopologyPreviewResponse.description: Response from the topology preview endpoint. Contains the derived physical network topology without creating a simulation or persisting any state.

CompatibilityEntry.description: Compatibility entry for a single MPI collective operation, listing allowed algorithms, the platform default, and which combinations require a power-of-two rank count.

operationType.description: MPI collective operation type this entry describes.

allowedAlgorithms.description: Algorithms valid for this operation type.

defaultAlgorithm.description: Platform default algorithm used when the caller omits the algorithm field.

powerOfTwoRequired.description: Algorithms in this list require the rank count to be a power of two. Empty array if no such constraint exists for this operation.

CompatibilityMatrixResponse.description: The full operation/algorithm compatibility matrix. Each entry describes which algorithms are valid for a given collective operation type, the platform default, and power-of-two constraints.

entries.description: One entry per supported operation type, in enum declaration order.

ChartDefinitionsResponse.description: The chart definitions stored on this platform, served under one schema version

schemaVersion.description: The chart-definition schema version every body in this response conforms to. A client pinned to a different version refuses the whole document rather than any single definition.

definitions.description: The stored definition bodies, verbatim and ordered by id. There is no per-element wrapper: each body carries its own top-level id.

items.description: One stored chart-definition body, served as-is. The server interprets only its top-level id and reads nothing else in it for meaning. The absence of a type is deliberate — a described type-less schema is what the Rust generators carry through as a raw JSON value — so this description is required and must not be removed.
